claims.statement: create_deep_agent is the SDK construction seam: it accepts caller-provided backend, middleware, subagents, checkpointer and store dependencies, composes its protected core and tail middleware stack around them, and DeepAgentState uses a DeltaChannel reducer for messages to limit checkpoint growth.

DeepAgentRuntime resolves subagents and approvals before graph construction, composes Talon tools and middleware before delegating graph compilation to create_deep_agent, snapshots the graph and turn context for invocation, and replaces runtime tools transactionally so a failed replacement leaves the previous graph active.

AsyncSubAgentMiddleware exposes start, check, update, cancel, and list tools for remote Agent Protocol tasks, persists task records in parent async_tasks state, and on async invocations polls unfinished tasks to add new status notifications while retrying failed status reads on a later check.

RubricMiddleware is inactive without a rubric, otherwise stores private grading bookkeeping, grades after the agent stops, loops to the model for revision feedback, and leaves the last model response intact for failed, grader-error, or iteration-limit outcomes so consumers must observe rubric state or events.

ConversationSaver wraps caller-owned checkpoint and archive stores, checkpoints before appending changed top-level scoped messages to the archive, makes archive failures retryable without a cross-store transaction, waits for both writes before propagating cancellation, and blocks deletion of active sessions.

Talon hook transcripts place parent and child projections under a hashed conversation owner directory guarded against symlinks and revocation-marker changes; TalonHooks loads a per-turn trusted snapshot, gives child subagents distinct identities, and validates interrupt ownership before memoizing hook responses.

Talon local subagents are loaded from AGENTS.md frontmatter, resolve exact tools from the current graph catalog, run with fresh context rather than fork mode, and TaskTools supplies the sole parent task tool to add validated per-task tools while compiling an isolated child graph with only applicable approvals.

SubAgentMiddleware projects a completed child into the parent as a ToolMessage, preferring structured_response JSON, then a final-message refusal notice, then the last non-empty AI text; it converts ModelRefusalError and refusal-bearing StructuredOutputValidationError during both sync and async task invocation, while re-raising other validation failures.

Async subagent completion projects the terminal remote message as content blocks, but emits an explicit no-output result or a string fallback for unconvertible messages and normalizes a terminal refusal block into the same actionable refusal notice used for delegated task results.

create_deep_agent appends ModelRefusalMiddleware at the tail after unsupported-content handling so caller fallback middleware can catch refusals first; by default a top-level refusal raises, while excluding the middleware leaves the refusal message observable.

MCPToolProvider uses refresh revisions to defer MCP loading until a later turn or forced reload, and DeepAgentRuntime compiles replacement tools before assigning its active graph, so failed reloads leave the prior graph usable.

MCPConfigStore exposes redacted, revisioned configuration and atomically applies a validated single-server replacement under a sidecar lock; automatic approval cannot reuse a redacted secret while changing a field that could redirect it.

BackgroundSubagents detaches ordinary main-agent task calls into owner-scoped, in-memory workers with capacity and ownership controls, but runs scheduled-turn delegation inline so the result is available in the same unattended turn.

Detached Talon workers use a distinct task thread, clear the authorization handler, disable approval-operator status, and convert approval interrupts, timeout, and failure into safe task results; results are acknowledged after parent consumption and can be requeued if host delivery is discarded.

SubagentControl keeps bounded metadata and coordinator message receipts outside graph state; only Talon-built local workers accept queued follow-ups, which are injected at the next model boundary without exposing tool arguments, outputs, or reasoning.

TalonHost starts the agent before channels and scheduler, unwinds partially started components in reverse order, and on shutdown cancels host work before stopping channels, scheduler, and runtime while isolating component-stop failures.

The Talon host transcribes ordinary inbound voice before media staging, preserving the original message on disabled, failed, or empty transcription and appending successful text with a voice_transcribed marker; local transcription converts audio to temporary WAV and caches a restricted-file Parakeet pipeline.

dcode's ServerProcess owns the local langgraph-dev subprocess lifecycle: it serializes startup, waits for health, cleans up incomplete startup including cancellation, and launches a separate POSIX process session with an owner-death pipe so the server does not outlive its manager.
